newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- TOP NATWEST MARKETS TEAM FACES SHAKE-UP

Chief executive of NatWest Markets, Martin Owen, is to unveil a new management structure and appoint a new chief operating officer, Peter Hall, who will assume day-to-day responsibility. Mr Owen is pushing for a move towards an American-style operating structure, especially after the rapid growth in the investments bank. He has denied suggestions that he is stepping back from the business.
-- PSBR BOOST FOR CHANCELLOR

Chancellor Kenneth Clarke will deliver the Budget against the backdrop of an unexpected improvement in the public finances brought about by strong growth and falling unemployment. Treasury projections will show that the public sector borrowing requirement is shrinking faster than anticipated six months ago. Since then, VAT receipts have rebounded and income tax receipts have started to climb. Figures will show that October was a good month for public finances, due to the usual concentration of corporation tax payments.
-- PRU CAST OFF BY SEAMEN'S FUND

Prudential Portfolio Managers has been ousted by the 2.3 billion stg Merchant Navy Officers Pension Fund as investment managers and has been replaced by the 13 billion dollar US-based investment group, First Quadrant. It is understood the fund appointed the consultancy Watson Wyatt to consider submissions from four investment management groups, including Prudential. The Pru has declined to comment.
THE TIMES
-- SHARE OPTIONS WORTH 80 MILLION STG HELD BY UTILITY DIRECTORS

Research by the Labour Party states that directors of privatised utilities are sitting on 80 million stg of paper profits on share options and could save 31 million stg if Prime Minister John Major achieves his aim of abolishing capital gains tax. The research suggests that the directors of National Power are sitting on profits from share options of 17.7 million stg. The total potential profit from options given to directors of privatised utilities stand at 80 million stg.
-- BRITAIN ALONE WILL MEET EU JOBS TARGET

According to a report by the European Commission on the UK labour market, Britain is likely to be the only country in Europe to meet the EU's target of halving its unemployment by 2000. Other conclusions of the report are more critical of Britain. These include growing wage inequalities, lack of flexibility and the minimum wage. Whitehall officials have intervened in the preparation of the report in an attempt to make its findings more acceptable.
-- DEUTSCHE FLOAT TO RAISE AN EXTRA ONE BILLION STG

The Deutsche Telekom offer is to increased by a further one billion stg after the floatation. Advisors to the group said an extra 90 million shares are expected to be sold within the next three weeks. Shares will begin trading on the New York and Frankfurt stock exchanges today. Advisors in New York confirmed that Telekom officials were counting on increasing the number of shares a second time because of the overwhelming demand for the offer.
THE GUARDIAN
-- GAS PAY-OUT PLAN TO AVOID POWER CUTS

A Government-backed scheme that plans to avoid power cuts in the run up to the next general election has come under fire by coal producers, PowerGen and protestors. The scheme compensates the operators of gas-fired power stations forced to switch to expensive fuels at times of high demand or when they choose to trade their cheaper gas supplies on the gas market. The Coal Producers Confederation said that the plans were "preposterous" and that gas-fired stations should hold the necessary fuel stocks at their own costs.
-- BANK WARNS OF SHOCKS IN STORE AS E-MONEY GAINS GLOBAL CURRENCY

A report by the Switzerland-based Bank for International Settlements has warned that banks and consumers in countries developing systems using electronic money will be vulnerable to widespread fraud, saying that criminals will be tempted by not only financial gain but also the chance to disrupt the system. The report warns that e-money will be so complex that monetary policy could be affected as central banks will find it harder to keep track of money supply.
-- GRANADA TO REVEAL ITS EXCLUSIVE STORY

Granada is set to reveal the results of its 3.9 billion stg January assault on Forte FTE.L when it reports full-year profits on Wednesday. Most analysts will be interested in what chairman Gerry Robinson has to say about the 17 Exclusive hotels which were formerly owned by Forte and have been up for sale for most of the year. Granada is forecast to report a 100 million stg improvement in profits.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BRITISH GAS BOOSTED BY TAKEOVER RUMOURS

Following a report that Shell has approached chairman of British Gas, Richard Giordano, with a takeover proposal has heightened speculation that a number of predators have been showing an interest in acquiring the group. There is no evidence of any imminent deal and British Gas and Shell have both refused to be drawn into denying or confirming the claimed talks. Sources familiar with the companies suggest that whatever discussions that might have taken place in the past are now dead and buried. If this is confirmed institutional shareholders in British Gas are likely to be angry it was not explored further.
-- RESELLERS THREATEN PHONE GIANTS

According to a report by Ovum, the telecommunications research group, telephone giants, such as British Telecom, face a massive explosion in price competition over the next 10 years from a host of bargain-basement operators that could take up a third of their international call businesses. The new firms are known as "resellers" and make their money by buying up bulk international call capacity from network operators at cost price and packing as many customers onto the lines as possible.
-- 500 MILLION STG QATAR ARMS DEAL BENEFITS UK FIRMS

British companies, British Aerospace, GKN, Vosper Thornycroft and Short Brothers, are sharing a 500 million stg arms deal signed in Qatar by Defence Secretary Michael Portillo and Sheik Ahmed bin Saif Al Thani, Qatar minister of state. The contract will help secure 500 jobs at Shorts Missile Systems and is the second large defence contract for Britain in a week. It is also the first large arms sale for Britain in the Gulf for years.
